title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: Amendment Charges Reflected in a Decided File
content:
## Principle

A review decision on a Dangerous Goods Acceptance file speaks for the whole file as it stands at the moment of deciding, and that includes its account. For the amendments on the file, the account has to be square with the declaration file: every signed amendment that the category's free allowance does not absorb is matched by an entry charged as an amendment fee. A decision cannot be given on a file whose account falls short of that match; such a file stays under review and no decision is entered.

## How the match is measured

- **Chargeable amendments:** the signed amendment declarations of the acceptance in excess of the category's free allowance, with zero as the floor.
- **Matching entries:** the entries on the acceptance's account that carry the amendment-fee charge code.
- **Square:** the matching entries are at least as many as the chargeable amendments.

## Worked cases (invented free allowance of 2)

| Signed amendments | Chargeable | Amendment-fee entries on the account | Square | Decision possible on this ground |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | 0 | yes | yes |
| 3 | 1 | 0 | no | no |
| 3 | 1 | 1 | yes | yes |
| 4 | 2 | 1 | no | no |

## Points of judgement

**Declarations awaiting signature sit on the file. Do they matter here?** No. Only signed amendments enter the count of chargeable amendments.

**The account holds a re-review fee but no amendment-fee entry, and one amendment is chargeable.** The file is not square: a re-review fee is not an amendment-fee entry.
